slides.say: Given: x is not equal to negative five. x y plus five y equals two x plus ten. What is y?
One equation with two letters, x and y, and they ask for one value. Some students say, one equation and two letters, it can't be solved. So they choose cannot be determined. That's the trap.
This is the case of more letters than equations. [short pause] We'll solve it by plugging in numbers, and then see why it works the math way.

If y has one value, it's the same for every allowed x. So I may choose x myself. Which x? Zero, because it makes every term with x equal to zero. And it's allowed, because the only condition is that x isn't negative five.
So x equals zero. x y is zero, and two x is zero. We're left with five y equals ten, so y is two.
With x equal to zero, y is two. So y is not negative five, and it's not negative two. Choice numbers one and three are out.
Two choices are left, two, and cannot be determined. If y changed when x changes, the answer would be cannot be determined. So the tie-breaker is a different x. Let's take x equals one.
With x equal to one, x y is just y, and two x is two. So y plus five y is six y, and two plus ten is twelve. Six y equals twelve, so y is two again.
Two examples gave the same y. That's a strong hint, but a few examples never prove always. So let's see why it's always two.
at: a few examples never prove always

slides.say: Now the math way. On the left, both terms contain y. We can write x y plus five y as y times the sum x plus five. Multiplying y by each part gives x y and five y again. On the right, both terms contain a factor of two. Two x plus ten is two times the sum x plus five. So both sides contain the same factor, x plus five.
at: We can write x y plus five y

slides.say: x plus five is not zero, because x is not negative five. So we may divide both sides by it, and y is two, for every allowed x. Choice number two is our answer.
at: x plus five is not zero
Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Now you see why they gave the condition. If x were negative five, both sides would be zero, and y could be anything. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
